problem.text: RMSNorm.forward flattened its input and restored its output shape through Python view operations even though the kernel already addresses contiguous rows.

reasoning.text: The edits are coupled: removing Python flattening requires the native wrapper to derive width from the last dimension and multiply all preceding dimensions into its row count.

impact.text: This removes Python shape bookkeeping and two view operations without changing the normalization kernel. Reduced CPU overhead is plausible, but no speedup was measured.

source_notes.text: The root runtime entry was read. It describes vectorized RMSNorm and records the non-float-as-half dtype classification; inspection of the parent and task diff shows that classification is carried over unchanged.

limitations: No extension build, GPU execution, numerical comparison or timing was performed.
The scalar check covers small contiguous shapes with Python integers; it does not establish strided-layout behavior, native integer-overflow behavior or GPU arithmetic.
The inspected native callers are RMSNorm.forward and extension tests; broader model entry-point compatibility was not exhaustively traced.

chapters.title: Move RMSNorm flattening bookkeeping into the native wrapper

claims.text: forward now allocates empty_like directly from the original input and returns that tensor directly. Output dtype selection, epsilon, weights and constant bias are unchanged; params remains unused and only loses its dict annotation.

Native validation now requires matching complete input/output shapes, last-axis width matching weight axis zero, and width divisible by four. The full-shape macro compares tensor sizes, not merely element counts.

The unchanged kernel launches one 1,024-thread block per flattened row. Four is the vector width of its half4/float4 loads and stores; each row computes x × (w + constant_bias) / sqrt(mean(x²) + epsilon), with float accumulation and separate half/float input-output instantiations.

A standard-library scalar transcription checked 255 positive shapes of ranks one through four: multiplying leading dimensions and using row × width plus four-element vector offsets covered contiguous storage exactly.

Whole-tree rms_norm search located the module wrapper and direct extension tests. The wrapper supplies all five arguments and creates matching output shapes. Tests use matching two-dimensional buffers, which agree with the revised shape convention, but their four-argument calls remain incompatible with the inspected five-argument native declaration.

findings.description: The native wrapper still treats every non-float dtype as half.
findings.trigger: Calling rms_norm with input or output other than float32 or float16 while satisfying its shape and weight checks.
findings.actual_behavior: Dispatch selects half pointers for non-float tensors; the final invalid-dtype branch cannot reject them.

verification.description: Compared unchanged dtype dispatch with the task diff and inspected located direct callers. RMSNorm.forward adds no dtype guard; tests supply only half/float.
verification.limits: No unsupported-dtype invocation or broader model workflow was executed.

findings.description: Existing direct extension tests omit constant_bias.
findings.trigger: Running test_rms_norm or its benchmark against the inspected native binding.
findings.expected_behavior: Tests invoke the five-argument RMSNorm interface.
findings.actual_behavior: All three test call sites pass only four arguments; the native declaration requires five and the located binding supplies no default.

verification.description: Compared all located extension calls with the declaration. The production Python wrapper supplies constant_bias; the task does not modify the tests.

annotation.summary: RMSNorm removes Python reshape bookkeeping by calculating flattened row counts natively; kernel arithmetic is unchanged and performance remains unmeasured.
